$comment: CS1: the single capability manifest. Every public /api* route belongs to exactly one capability (tests/api-capabilities-manifest.test.js). It ships in the image and GET /release lists its ids. docs/API-ROUTES.md and docs/CAPABILITIES.md are generated from it (npm run docs:api). knowshowgo-client and OSLO vendor a copy and check their methods and skill docs against it.

audiences.agent: OSLO, OpenClaw and any SDK or MCP caller: every route has a client method or a stated reason in noClient
audiences.experimental: not for agents yet; no client method required

capabilities.title: Release and health
capabilities.summary: What this server is: version, prefixes, token auth, MCP, and the capability list.
capabilities.whenToUse: Read once at start (`get_release_manifest`) to learn the server version and which capabilities it has; never on every turn.

capabilities.title: Owner tokens (KT1)
capabilities.summary: Issue, list and revoke per-owner API tokens. With the access gate on, every other /api* call needs one.
capabilities.whenToUse: Give each owner (user) their own token and send it on every call (`set_auth_token` per client, `for_owner({ auth_token })` per owner, or `auth_token` per call). A 401 means no or a revoked token: get a new one; never retry anonymously.
capabilities.tokenNote: The gate lets these through (`open`); the handler itself needs the admin secret (`x-ksg-admin`) or the owner’s own bearer token, so a token is issued by an operator or minted from an existing one.

capabilities.title: Semantic memory (remember / recall / ask)
capabilities.summary: Turn chat into claims with provenance and read them back as answers with evidence.
capabilities.whenToUse: Remember what the user said (`semantic_remember`), recall before answering (`semantic_recall`), `semantic_ask` for an answer that says what it rests on; `semantic_correct` when the user corrects a stored value.

noClient.GET /semantic/events/:uuid: immutable MemoryEvent read; `semantic_recall` returns the events an answer used

capabilities.title: Episodes and events
capabilities.summary: What happened, as typed events with roles; episodes recalled by meaning.
capabilities.whenToUse: Record a run or an occurrence as an event (`record_event`); `recall_episodes` to find similar past situations before planning.

capabilities.title: Facts with a lifecycle
capabilities.summary: Owner facts that go candidate → verified by confirmation, corrected by a new version.
capabilities.whenToUse: Store a user statement as a fact (`add_fact`); a model guess stays a candidate until `confirm_fact`; `correct_fact` supersedes, never overwrites. On a claim in a contested set (KSG-2), confirm keeps that side and correct sets a new value: either way a new version supersedes every side (owner for a private set, admin token for a public one).

capabilities.title: Assertions and beliefs
capabilities.summary: Weighted claims with votes, reinforcement, contradiction and retraction; any claim returns why it is believed (sources with tier and speaker, version chain, contested peers, model or Logic IR rule, status with the reason). The contradiction inbox lists the open contested sets (KS-TIER) with both sides’ sources and tiers.
capabilities.whenToUse: Prefer propositions (KG-P1) for new claims; use assertions to reinforce, contradict or retract an existing claim with a reason. To answer "why do we believe this?" about one value, `explain_claim(uuid)` (GET /assertions?uuid=…&why=true). To review disagreements, `list_contradictions()` (GET /assertions?contested=true); resolve one with `confirm_fact(side)` or `correct_fact(side, {obj})`, which write a new superseding version, never a delete.

capabilities.title: Propositions (KG-P1) and proposals (CE3d)
capabilities.summary: Claims as subject–predicate–object over three concept uuids, each with a provenance tier; model-made claims are proposals until a public source confirms them.
capabilities.whenToUse: Write a relational claim with `assert_proposition`. A model inference is sent with `source: "llm:…"` (tier inferred): it is a proposal, never a fact. `reconcile_inferred_propositions` checks proposals about a name against higher-tier claims; cite the tier in answers.

capabilities.title: Typed property values (TB2 / KV1)
capabilities.summary: A closed list of value types (url, uuid ref, number, date, time, …), declared properties with cardinality and range, a prototype’s field list.
capabilities.whenToUse: Before writing a property, read its type (`list_value_types`, `get_prototype_fields`); declare a missing one with `declare_predicate` (an existing name is returned, not duplicated).

capabilities.title: Topic articles and amendments (TB2)
capabilities.summary: A topic read like an article: fields from its prototypes and claims, the current value and every other version with its provenance; amend by adding a claim.
capabilities.whenToUse: Read a topic for a person (`get_article`); amend with `amend_article` and `replaces_claim` to version a value (the old one stays readable). Needs a signed-in owner (401 otherwise).

capabilities.title: Concepts and lookup (CE3a / CE3c)
capabilities.summary: Find, create, resolve, merge and unmerge concepts; look an unknown term up in Wikidata (links written as propositions) and ConceptNet (`commonly_a` edges as weighted, attributed claims).
capabilities.whenToUse: Resolve a name before creating (`resolve_concept`, then `find_or_create_concept`); `lookup_concept` for a public term the graph lacks; merge duplicates with `merge_concepts` (reversible with `unmerge_concept`).

capabilities.title: Topics, tags and concept objects
capabilities.summary: Topics as named concept objects; tag resolution and suggestions.
capabilities.whenToUse: Resolve a free-text tag to a topic (`resolve_topic_tag`) before creating a new one; `suggest_concept_objects` for candidates.

capabilities.title: Knowledge search (KL2 vectors, CM1 where), query, grounding
capabilities.summary: Semantic search over knowledge (vector rows by default), typed constraints over instances (`where`), structured query, grounding and slot resolution.
capabilities.whenToUse: Use `search_knowledge` for a fuzzy question. For a typed one ("the current requirement for this portal", "dogs with black ears whose name starts with H, not German Shepherds") pass `where: { type, all, any, not }`: `results` holds only instances whose every constraint is known to hold on stated claims, each with the claim ids, tiers and statuses behind it; instances that are unknown on a constraint come back apart under `unknown` and must never be reported as matches. For joins across several things prefer `bind_pattern`. `ground` to tie a phrase to known concepts.

capabilities.title: Verification
capabilities.summary: Check a claim or an answer against stored evidence; unknown beats invented.
capabilities.whenToUse: Before stating a fact as true, `verify_answer`; "unknown" means say you do not know.

capabilities.title: Entities: beliefs, evidence, explanation
capabilities.summary: Everything known about one thing: types, properties, beliefs, evidence, explanation and a one-trip hydration.
capabilities.whenToUse: To answer "why do you think that" use `explain_entity` / `get_evidence`; `hydrate_entity` for a full projection in one call.

capabilities.title: Logic over the graph
capabilities.summary: Pattern binding, transitive closure, relational joins, rules with derivations you can read back.
capabilities.whenToUse: Prefer `bind_pattern` over free text for relational questions ("who works at Contoso"); `close_relation` for chains (part_of, subclass_of); `evaluate_joins` across two relations; `get_derivation_tree` to show why.

capabilities.title: Prototypes, matching and typicality (SX1)
capabilities.summary: Categories as a definition plus exemplars and a centroid; match a thing to categories with graded typicality; membership with evidence.
capabilities.whenToUse: `match_prototypes` to type an unknown thing (ranked, with typicality); `check_membership` for a yes/no with evidence — typicality is not membership; `assimilate_exemplar` to add a confirmed member.

capabilities.title: Taxonomy reader (DH1 duplicates)
capabilities.summary: The category tree, a prototype’s definition, centroid, properties and exemplars, a node’s propositions; duplicate prototype names.
capabilities.whenToUse: `get_taxonomy` to browse; `get_taxonomy_prototype` for what a category means; `get_taxonomy_duplicates` before seeding a prototype by name.

capabilities.title: Objects, categories, ORM and composites
capabilities.summary: Typed objects upserted by identity, object categories, ORM-style instances, composites and memory roles.
capabilities.whenToUse: Use `upsert_object` for a record with a stable identity (a company, a portal); `resolve_object` before writing.

noClient.POST /composites/:uuid/components/:compo: legacy /api only; composites are rewritten by `create_composite`

capabilities.title: Procedures (KL1 search, RP1 lifecycle, versions)
capabilities.summary: Stored procedures with runs, versions (candidate → validated → promoted → retired) and lifecycle-safe search.
capabilities.whenToUse: Recall with `search_verified_procedures` (verified only) or `search_procedures` (verified + drafts; `include: "retired"|"all"` only to audit). Follow a retired hit’s `replacedBy`. Record every run (`record_procedure_run`) with an independent outcome signal.

capabilities.title: Knowledge packs (PK1)
capabilities.summary: A versioned bundle of prototypes, procedures and facts as one `ksg-pack/1` file with a name, semver version, license, source and per-item provenance.
capabilities.whenToUse: Export a chosen set to hand a workflow to another store (`export_pack`); install a pack to receive one (`install_pack`, with `dry_run: true` first to see the plan; it writes nothing). Export is read-only: an item you may not read answers as a missing one, your own private items leave only with the explicit opt-in `include_private: true` (off by default), and secret-shaped values are redacted. A pack grants no trust: installed procedures are your private candidates with no runs (never recall them as trusted until a verified run), installed facts are third-party candidates until you confirm them, and a newer version supersedes, never deletes.

capabilities.title: Channels, ratings, associations, market
capabilities.summary: Social layer: channel messages and feeds, ratings, associations, market matches.
capabilities.whenToUse: Only for multi-agent or marketplace flows; not needed for personal memory.

capabilities.title: Private payment vault
capabilities.summary: Owner-only payment records; never embedded, never returned to another owner.
capabilities.whenToUse: Only through OSLO’s vault tools with an approval gate; never put a card in a prompt.

capabilities.title: Agent capability model (experimental)
capabilities.summary: Provider-neutral capability declarations and the composable runtime schema.
capabilities.whenToUse: Not for agents yet; no SDK method.

capabilities.title: Feedback tickets
capabilities.summary: Bug, idea or question tickets filed by MCP callers and OSLO’s report button; listed with the admin token.
capabilities.whenToUse: File a ticket when KSG answers wrongly (MCP `feedback` tool).

noClient.POST /feedback: filed by the MCP `feedback` tool and OSLO’s report button

capabilities.title: Seeds (schema.org, SX1 exemplars, primitives)
capabilities.summary: Idempotent seeds: schema.org prototypes, Wikidata exemplars and centroids, agent and logic primitives.
capabilities.whenToUse: Operators and boot only; agents read the result through taxonomy and prototypes.

capabilities.title: Admin and ops
capabilities.summary: Access-gate counters, graph stats, usage, search-miss ledger and lookup drain.
capabilities.whenToUse: Operators with the admin secret; not for agents.

capabilities.title: Deploy probes
capabilities.summary: Echo endpoints used once by deploy checks. Flagged: candidates for removal (backlog).
capabilities.whenToUse: Never from an agent.

features.title: Claims as propositions over concept uuids
features.whenToUse: Every relational claim; the subject, predicate and object are concept uuids, not strings.

features.title: Model proposals confirmed by a public source
features.whenToUse: Propose facts via proposals (tier inferred); never assert a model inference as a fact. Stats count proposals, confirmations and contradictions.

features.title: Pattern binding
features.whenToUse: Prefer over free-text search for any relational question.

features.title: Transitive closure
features.whenToUse: Chains: part_of, subclass_of, located_in.

features.title: Relational joins
features.whenToUse: A question that crosses two relations ("employees of companies in Contoso’s region").

features.title: Membership with evidence (typicality is not membership)
features.whenToUse: Yes/no category membership; read `evidence`, not the score.

features.title: Prototype matching with typicality
features.whenToUse: Type an unknown thing; ranked categories with typicality.

features.title: Seeded exemplars and centroids (schema.org + Wikidata)
features.whenToUse: Categories start with a meaning and members; read them in `get_taxonomy_prototype`.

features.title: schema.org prototypes
features.whenToUse: Operators seed; agents use the categories through taxonomy and prototypes.

features.title: Taxonomy tree, prototype and node views
features.whenToUse: Browse categories; read a node’s propositions with status, truth and provenance.

features.title: Wikidata lookup writes propositions
features.whenToUse: A public term the graph lacks; links come back as is_a / subclass_of / part_of claims with the source.

features.title: ConceptNet commonly_a common sense
features.whenToUse: Common-sense edges (`commonly_a`) are weighted, attributed and never facts about a specific person.

features.title: Procedure search scoped and indexed
features.whenToUse: Recall a procedure for a goal and site.

features.title: Retired procedures are opt-in
features.whenToUse: Default search leaves retired procedures out; `include: "retired"|"all"` only to audit.

features.title: Vector rows for concept and knowledge search
features.whenToUse: Nothing to change in the call; search is faster and reads the vector rows.

features.title: Typed property values
features.whenToUse: Write values in their declared type (url, uuid ref, number, date, time…); a wrong type is refused with 422.

features.title: Version chains and amendments
features.whenToUse: Amend, never overwrite: `replaces_claim` keeps the old value readable as a version.

features.title: Per-owner tokens, 401 at the edge
features.whenToUse: One token per owner; a 401 is a missing or revoked token, not a server fault.

features.title: Supersede, never delete (replacedBy)
features.whenToUse: A duplicate or outdated record is superseded with `replacedBy`; follow it, and never ask KSG to delete.

features.title: Why do we believe this? (KSG-1)
features.whenToUse: Before relying on or showing a value, read its `why`: a `contested` or `candidate` status means say so, not state it as fact; cite `sources` and their tiers.

features.title: Contradiction inbox (KSG-2)
features.whenToUse: Disagreements are a review queue, not last-write-wins: list them, show both sides with their tiers, and resolve by confirm or correct (a new version); never pick a side silently.

features.title: Centroid moves: confirmed, versioned, isolated (R6b)
features.whenToUse: Fold a confirmed member into a category with `assimilate_exemplar` and say what confirmed it (`evidence: { kind: owner_confirmed | verified_run | validated_assimilation, ref }`). A membership resting on a candidate or model-inferred claim is refused (409 M006); a private exemplar never moves a shared centroid (409 M007). Every move keeps the state it replaced as a version (`taxonomy` prototype view → `centroid.history`).

features.title: Grounding by centroid, with a margin (R6a)
features.whenToUse: Ground a token by `ground({ method: 'centroid', term })`: the top candidates among readable prototypes (definition + running centroid) and concepts, each with its similarity, and the margin between the first two. Below the threshold (`margin`, else `KSG_CENTROID_MARGIN`, else 0.05) the answer is `ambiguous`: ask the person or learn the word; never pick silently. `items: [{ term, expect? }]` runs a labelled list (top-k, margins, rank of the expected answer) for threshold experiments. Read-only.

features.title: Typed constraints in knowledge search (CM1)
features.whenToUse: Add `where` to `search_knowledge` when the question names a type and property values. Constraints are true / false / unknown per instance; `not` of unknown is unknown; a candidate or model-inferred claim is never a match. Report `results` as matches, `unknown` as "not established", and an empty `results` as "no verified match", never the nearest text hit.
